page: Amazon Web Services m6a.12xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose compute instance based on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at 3.6 GHz, offering 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs via two threads per core. The instance provides 192.0 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware cryptographic acceleration is enabled via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI instruction sets, alongside AVX vector extensions, though AVX-512 and AMX instructions are absent.

The platform does not include local instance storage, requiring attached Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) volumes for persistent and root filesystem needs. Network performance is anchored by a baseline bandwidth of 19 Gbps, supporting moderate-to-high data transfer requirements across cloud environments. There are no discrete GPUs provisioned on this configuration, focusing resource delivery entirely on traditional central processing workloads.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-threaded and computational throughput, with the instance placing in the top 25 percent for stress-ng multi-core tests (71,754.38) and PassMark CPU ratings (54,515.26). Encryption routines benefit directly from hardware instructions, achieving a PassMark CPU encryption score of 56,919.89. Memory performance benchmarks register solidly, including a PassMark memory score of 2,860.38, while uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 66.79 GB/sec and write bandwidth reaches 32.47 GB/sec. Application benchmarks reflect mid-tier throughput for Redis operations at 52.31 million operations per second and static web serving at 20.37 GB/sec.

The m6a.12xlarge delivers predictable scale across balanced multi-core deployments. It offers strong compute density per resource allocation for general-purpose workloads, avoiding the cost profile of memory-maximized or specialized accelerator tiers. Suitable production applications include distributed enterprise microservices, intermediate data transformation pipelines, mid-sized relational and in-memory caches, software compilation clusters, and continuous integration and deployment workers.
description: Amazon Web Services m6a.12xlarge is a general-purpose Nitro-based cloud instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor running at 3.6 GHz. It offers 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores and incorporates 192.0 GB of DDR4 system memory, reflecting a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The architecture lacks integrated local disk storage and discrete GPUs, operating with remote block storage and a baseline network throughput of 19 Gbps. Performance benchmarks demonstrate high compute capability, scoring in the upper 25 percent for stress-ng multi-core testing, PassMark CPU ratings, and cryptographic throughput. Memory bandwidth and standard application tests, such as Redis operations and static web serving, show steady mid-range execution. With balanced compute and memory distribution, the m6a.12xlarge is well positioned for multi-threaded enterprise services, backend application hosting, build farms, and structured batch processing workloads.
